* There are some other considerations, please confirm that you have read the help first.

On Android 11 or above, you can enable Wireless debugging and start AndroidControl directly from your device, without connecting to a computer.

Please view the step-by-step guide first.
Before Android 11, connecting to a computer is required to enable Wireless debugging.

Please enable \"Wireless debugging\" in \"Developer options\". \"Wireless debugging\" is automatically disabled when network changes.\n\nNote, do not disable \"Developer options\" or \"USB debugging\", or AndroidControl will be stopped.
Please try to disable and enable \"Wireless debugging\" if it keeps searching.
Port is an integer ranging from 1 to 65535.
Can\'t connect to wireless debugging service.
Wireless debugging is not enabled.\nNote, before Android 11, to enable wireless debugging, computer connection is a must.

Please start paring by the following steps: \"Developer Options\" - \"Wireless debugging\" - \"Pairing device using pairing code\".\n\nAfter the pairing process starts, you will able to input the pairing code.
The system requires the pairing dialog always visible, using split-screen mode is the only way to let this app and system dialog visible at the same time.
Could not read or save the wireless debugging credentials. Unlock the device and try again.
Reset the saved wireless debugging key? You will need to enter a new pairing code. Other app settings will be kept.
Please go through the pairing step first.
A notification from AndroidControl will help you complete the pairing.
Enter \"Developer options\" - \"Wireless debugging\". Tap \"Pair device with pairing code\", you will see a six-digit code.
Enter the code in the notification to complete pairing.
The pairing process needs you to interact with a notification from AndroidControl. Please allow AndroidControl to post notifications.
MIUI users may need to switch notification style to \"Android\" from \"Notification\" - \"Notification shade\" in system settings.
Otherwise, you may not able to enter paring code from the notification.
Please note, left part of the \"Wireless debugging\" option is clickable, tapping it will open a new page. Only turing on the switch on the right is incorrect.
Back to AndroidControl and start AndroidControl.
AndroidControl needs to access local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses foreground service as standard. Please disable battery optimization features for AndroidControl on such systems.

Your device manufacturer has restricted adb permissions and apps using AndroidControl will not work properly.

Usually, this limitation can be lifted by adjusting some options in "Developer options". Please read the help for details on how to do this.

You may need to restart AndroidControl for the operation to take effect.
The permission of adb is limited

It\'s highly possible that your device manufacturer limits the permission of adb.

There may be a solution for your system in this document.
Run commands through AndroidControl in terminal apps you like
First, Export files to any where you want. You will find two files, %1$s and %2$s.

If there are files with the same name in the selected folder, they will be deleted.\n\nThe export function uses SAF (Storage Access Framework). It\'s reported that MIUI breaks the functions of SAF. If you are using MIUI, you may have to extract the file from AndroidControl\'s apk or download from GitHub.
Then, use any text editor to open and edit %1$s.
For example, if you want to use AndroidControl in %1$s, you should replace %2$s with %3$s (%4$s is the package name of %1$s).
Finally, move the files to somewhere where your terminal app can access, you will be able to use %1$s to run commands through AndroidControl.
Some tips: grant execute permission to %1$s and add it to %2$s, you will able to use %1$s directly.

With %1$s, in any terminal app, you can connect to and interact with the shell runs by AndroidControl.
